provenance: Real ESA Anomaly Dataset (ESA-ADB) telemetry, Mission1 lightweight channels 41-46. Kotowski et al., 'European Space Agency Dataset and Benchmark for Real-World Anomaly Detection in Spacecraft Time Series', Journal of Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR), 2026 (earlier version: arXiv:2406.17826). Data: De Canio, Kotowski & Haskamp, 'ESA Anomaly Dataset', Zenodo record 12528696 (2024), CC BY 3.0 IGO. Missions are anonymised Mission1/2/3; they are not named Sentinel anything. Resampled to 30s, by ESA-ADB's zero-order hold, and z-scored with the mean and standard deviation of the unlabelled training rows, by the training script's own prepare(). These are 128 of the 7,363,910 windows in the held-out test window, the half of the 14,728,319-step timeline from 2007-01-01 in the corpus's anonymised calendar, ESA-ADB's own Mission1 split, drawn at random from the 7,208,289 that touch no label, inputs and target, and kept in time order; the model trained on none of them. The page's CKKS check scores the OPS-SAT student on 529 OPS-SAT-AD segments, not these windows.
split: windows drawn at random from the held-out test half's windows that touch no label, ESA-ADB's own Mission1 split from 2007-01-01
attribution: Kotowski et al., 'European Space Agency Dataset and Benchmark for Real-World Anomaly Detection in Spacecraft Time Series', Journal of Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR), 2026 (earlier version: arXiv:2406.17826). Data: De Canio, Kotowski & Haskamp, 'ESA Anomaly Dataset', Zenodo record 12528696 (2024), CC BY 3.0 IGO.
modifications: Channels 41 to 46 of ESA-ADB Mission1, resampled to 300 s, forward-filled, z-scored with the training window's mean and standard deviation, and cut into 250-step windows; 128 windows drawn at random from the held-out test window (the last 30 percent of the timeline), with each window's next-step values as targets, rounded to 4 decimals.

input.layout: samples[i] is 250 timesteps x 6 channels at 30s cadence, row-major, already resampled and z-scored

expected.note: Mean absolute error of the next-step forecast in z-score units, measured here with onnxruntime on exactly these windows as shipped. persistence_mae is what predicting no change would score, so a reader can tell whether the model is doing anything. On these windows the median absolute error is 0.2180 against 0.3029 for no change, and the model's own mean error is the lower on 99 of 128: where the two means disagree, a few large misses carry the first. Over all 7,363,910 test windows the same graph scores 0.8386 against persistence 0.3531, and over the 7,208,289 that touch no label, the pool these windows come from, 0.3044 against 0.3514. The forecaster never trains on a labelled row, and its forecast is far off where the telemetry is anomalous - which is how it detects - so labelled rows dominate the first mean.
